title: SAGA: Score-Weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment for Low-Resource Nordic Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2608.06179v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Preference optimisation has proven effective for improving large language models but typically relies on costly human preference annotations. Extending these methods to morphologically rich, low-resource languages remains challenging because such annotations are scarce. We present SAGA (Score-weighted Adaptive Generation Alignment), a parser-guided preference optimisation framework that replaces human labels with dependency-parser supervision. SAGA converts parser judgements into preference pairs for delta-DPO, combines parser quality with lexical diversity in a composite reward, filters low-information pairs using a reward-gap criterion, and monitors reward hacking to maintain reliable supervision. Across Danish, Icelandic, and Norwegian Bokm{\aa}l using GPT-SW3-1.3B, SAGA consistently improves grammatical quality without requiring human preference labels. Danish parse success increases from 69.0% to 93.8%, Icelandic achieves a +4.5

translated_title: SAGA：面向低资源北欧语言模型的分数加权自适应生成对齐
translated_abstract: 偏好优化已被证明能有效改进大型语言模型，但通常依赖昂贵的人工偏好标注。将这些方法扩展到形态丰富、资源稀缺的语言仍具挑战性，因为此类标注稀缺。我们提出了SAGA（分数加权自适应生成对齐），一种解析器引导的偏好优化框架，用依赖解析器监督替代人工标签。SAGA将解析器判断转换为delta-DPO的偏好对，在复合奖励中结合解析质量与词汇多样性，利用奖励差距标准过滤低信息对，并监控奖励黑客以维持可靠的监督。在丹麦语、冰岛语和挪威博克马尔语上，使用GPT-SW3-1.3B，SAGA持续提升语法质量，无需人工偏好标签。丹麦语解析成功率从69.0%提升至93.8%，冰岛语实现+4.5的提升。
tldr: 本文提出SAGA框架，利用依赖解析器监督替代人工偏好标注，通过偏好优化显著提升低资源北欧语言的语法质量，无需人工标签。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes SAGA, a parser-guided preference optimization framework that replaces human preference labels with dependency-parser supervision, significantly improving grammatical quality in low-resource Nordic languages without human annotations.
